title: Grateful Dead Live at Easttown Theatre on 1971-10-24
source: Master Soundboard Reel > Cassette > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a pleasant hiss but clear overall; a high‑energy 1971 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star and stellar China>Rider.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a classic early‑’71 Dead performance – the band is tight, the setlist flows beautifully and songs like Dark Star, China > Rider, Black Peter and Candyman shine. While the soundboard source has a noticeable hiss and occasional drop‑outs, the mix remains clear enough to enjoy the inspired playing of Garcia, Lesh, Weir, Keith and Bill.

ai_rating.rationale: 22 detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4‑5 stars; musical performance is praised as exceptional while recording issues are minor, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable hiss and a few early cut‑offs/drop‑outs mentioned, but overall clear mix; the organ/piano is well captured and the balance is solid.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong, cohesive setlist with smooth transitions; early‑’71 material flows naturally and the rare Keith organ adds fresh texture.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his jamming on Playin', crushing leads throughout Dark Star, and overall tight guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for “off‑the‑chart” bass licks in China>Rider and Dark Star, with high‑register notes that wow reviewers.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for his humorous stage banter and strong contributions to China>Rider, essentially acting as a second lead guitarist.
band_member_comments.Keys: Rare Keith on organ/piano is called “sweet”, “honky‑tonk”, and a fresh injection of energy into the band.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (Billy) described as kick‑ass and solid, anchoring the band's tightness.
